references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 19:21|Matthew 19:21] recounts the same conversation where Jesus tells the rich man to sell all he owns, give to the poor, and follow him.
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 10:21|Mark 10:21] states that Jesus looked at the rich man with love and told him to sell everything, give to the poor, and follow him.

In [ref:Luk 12:33|Luke 12:33], Jesus gives a similar exhortation: "Sell what you own and give the money to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in heaven."
In [ref:Luk 14:33|Luke 14:33], Jesus says that no one can be his disciple without giving up everything they own, emphasizing the requirement of total surrender.
In [ref:Matt 6:19-21|Matthew 6:19-21], Jesus speaks about storing up treasures in heaven rather than on earth, which directly relates to the promise of "treasure in heaven" in this verse.

Paul urges the rich in [ref:1 Tim 6:17-19|1 Timothy 6:17-19] to be generous and share with others, so that they store up a treasure as a solid foundation for the future – echoing Jesus' words to the rich man.
In [ref:Apg 2:44-45|Acts 2:44-45], the first Christians sold their property and possessions and shared with everyone who was in need, in line with Jesus' call to the rich man.
In [ref:Apg 4:34-35|Acts 4:34-35], believers sold their properties and laid the money at the apostles' feet, a practical expression of what Jesus asked the rich man to do.
In [ref:Luk 5:11|Luke 5:11], the disciples left everything and followed Jesus, an example of the total commitment required by Jesus when he spoke to the rich man.
In [ref:Luk 5:27-28|Luke 5:27-28], Levi left everything and followed Jesus – yet another example of giving up wealth to follow Christ.
In [ref:Fil 3:7-8|Philippians 3:7-8], Paul counts everything as loss in order to gain Christ, reflecting the radical demand Jesus makes to give up earthly wealth for heavenly values.

In [ref:Ordsp 19:17|Proverbs 19:17] it is written that whoever shows kindness to the poor lends to the Lord, who will repay them – an Old Testament background for the promise of treasure in heaven through giving to the poor.
